statement: You are given a list of words, written in words as a single comma-separated string.

Word a is a predecessor of word b if inserting exactly one letter anywhere in a, without changing the order of its other letters, produces b. A chain is a sequence of words in which each word is a predecessor of the next.
Return the length of the longest chain that can be built from the given words. A single word is a chain of length 1.

examples.explanation: a → ba → bca → bdca: each step inserts one letter.
All five words form one chain: xb → xbc → cxbc → pcxbc → pcxbcf.

"dbqca" is one letter longer than "abcd", but removing any one of its letters never leaves "abcd" (the letters are in a different order). Neither word extends the other, so the longest chain is a single word.

constraints: Words contain only lowercase English letters
